title: The Last Garden
premise: Rosalind Dunmore, a runaway apprentice hiding in the smuggler's roads of the Thornfell mountains, discovers that the old gods—erased from history by a conquering empire—are waking and answering prayers again, and that Rosalind's own forgotten memories are the key to their return. Hunted by the empire's memory-eating Inquisitors and bound by a bargain they never knowingly made, Rosalind must choose between erasing themselves to stay safe and reclaiming a true name that will make them visible to every power in the land. With the help of Sera, an ex-Inquisitor who fell in love with the person she was sent to erase, Rosalind seeks the Last Garden, a door out of a country whose true history has been devoured. In the end, Rosalind reopens the Garden not as an escape but as a seed vault of memory, sacrificing their own remembered past so the old gods—and the country that no longer exists—can be born again, while Sera chooses exile at their side.
about_author: Astrid Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, forgetting, and the people who live in the gaps between maps.

chapters.title: Salt on the Mountain Road
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Smuggling moon-herb through a Thornfell pass, Rosalind notices wildflowers blooming out of season where an old shrine once stood—a sign the erased gods are stirring. The beat is wary competence masking loneliness; Rosalind has spent six years being no one, and something in the mountains just said their name.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Ran
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, POV Rosalind. We learn of hedge-witch Maren, the apprenticeship, the night Rosalind fled after Maren tried to burn a page of Rosalind's memory. Present-day: Rosalind returns to find Maren's cottage ransacked and Maren gone. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Inquisitors Eat
chapters.summary: POV Sera Vane, Inquisitor of the Ministry of Continuity, arrives in the valley hunting 'anomalous recollections.' She carries a ledger of names to be unmade—including one half-erased entry: R—— D——. Beat: cold duty beginning to crack as she interviews villagers who weep without knowing why.

chapters.title: Prayer Answered Badly
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Desperate for news of Maren, Rosalind prays at the blooming shrine—an act that hasn't worked in two hundred years. Something answers, speaking in Rosalind's own childhood voice. It asks for its name back. Beat: terror and longing entwined; invisibility is ending whether Rosalind likes it or not.

chapters.title: The Girl with the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Sera tracks Rosalind to a smuggler's inn; instead of arresting them, she hesitates—the half-erased name matches a face from her own missing childhood. They strike an uneasy truce over cards. Beat: two liars recognizing each other, attraction flickering under suspicion.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Instruction
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Following Maren's hidden notes, Rosalind learns the truth: the empire didn't conquer the country of Velthmere—it ate it, god by god, memory by memory, and Rosalind is a 'keystone,' a child ritually loaded with the last intact memory of the nation. Beat: identity shattered; Rosalind's whole self is someone else's archive.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Ordered to deliver Rosalind to the capital, Sera instead burns her orders—but her superior, Inquisitor-General Corvane, anticipated it. A chase through a pass that exists only on smuggler maps. Beat: betrayal of the Ministry made real; Sera commits fully to treason for love she won't yet name.

chapters.title: Gods in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Sheltering in drowned Velthmere ruins beneath a reservoir, Rosalind meets the god of thresholds, small and starving, wearing shapes borrowed from Rosalind's memories. It confirms the Last Garden is real—and that Corvane intends to eat Rosalind's keystone memory to kill the gods forever. Beat: wonder curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Captured briefly by Corvane, Sera is offered absolution and her own stolen childhood in exchange for delivering Rosalind. He shows her a single restored memory: a garden gate, a girl's hand in hers. Beat: temptation at its most intimate—the enemy holds Sera's own heart in escrow.

chapters.title: Confession at the Fireline
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Escaping together, Sera confesses everything, including the original order: she was assigned Rosalind's file years ago and chose to forget she'd refused it. Rosalind's fury nearly ends the alliance. Beat: love against duty made explicit—Sera chose Rosalind over herself long ago, badly.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In a free-town print shop, an old mapmaker recognizes the keystone sigil and reveals the Garden's location: it moves, and only someone carrying Velthmere's memory can see its door. Beat: hope with a price—Rosalind must stop running and start remembering, which the Inquisitors can feel like a beacon.

chapters.title: Every Prayer Is a Signal Fire
chapters.summary: POV Sera. As Rosalind deliberately reclaims memories, prayers ignite across the mountains; Corvane unleashes the Unremembering, a wave that hollows whole villages. Sera teaches Rosalind to shield memories inside shared moments between the two of them. Beat: intimacy as armor; love becomes literal survival technique.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Dead
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Passing through a village emptied by the Unremembering, Rosalind finds mourners standing at graves they cannot name. Against all strategy, Rosalind gives one grieving woman back her daughter's name. Beat: compassion versus caution; the cost of visibility accepted willingly.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Glass Lake
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Corvane's elite catch them crossing a frozen lake; Sera duels her former mentor while Rosalind holds the ice's memory solid beneath their feet. Sera kills him and is sick afterward. Beat: the point of no return—Sera can never go home, and stops wanting to.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Was Before
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The recovered memories crest: Rosalind was not merely an archive but the last child consecrated at the Garden, given up by parents who chose a nation's survival over their daughter's selfhood. Beat: rage and grief at being used as a vessel; identity must be claimed, not just recovered.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Guided by the threshold god, they reach the moving door of the Last Garden—but it opens onto the moment of Velthmere's fall, replaying endlessly. To enter, someone must carry the complete memory through, and be changed irreversibly. Beat: awe and dread at the threshold itself.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Corvane arrives with the full Ministry, offering Rosalind oblivion as mercy. Sera stands between them and speaks her true allegiance aloud, breaking her own Ministry conditioning. Battle among the Garden's outer hedges. Beat: love declared publicly at gunpoint; duty inverted.

chapters.title: The Eating of Names
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Corvane begins devouring the Garden's memories directly; the gods gutter out one by one. Rosalind realizes the keystone memory isn't a weapon but a seed—and seeds must be planted, not hoarded. Beat: clarity under fire; the plan reverses from escape to sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Garden Opens
chapters.summary: Climax, POV Rosalind. Rosalind walks into the heart of the Garden and releases the complete memory of Velthmere—not keeping it, letting it pour into the land, the gods, the villagers, even Corvane. The dead country blooms back into existence around them. Beat: transcendence through surrender of self.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Returned Nation
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Velthmere remembers itself; the Ministry collapses as everyone recalls what was taken. Corvane, now holding every memory he ever ate, wanders off hollowed by grief he finally understands. Sera searches the ruins for Rosalind. Beat: victory shadowed by loss—did Rosalind survive giving everything away?

chapters.title: Someone New Under an Old Sky
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind survived, but the archived memories are gone—they are, for the first time, only themselves, with a future unwritten. The returned gods offer gratitude and a home. Rosalind instead chooses the open road. Beat: quiet rebirth; identity chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Two Travelers, One Map
chapters.summary: POV alternating, closing chapter. Sera catches up to Rosalind at the crossroads out of the mountains, carrying nothing but a blank ledger. Together they walk toward a country being reborn, mapping what returns. Final beat: love freely chosen after duty is done; memory as something you plant, not carry.
